name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: Long diversified AI-infra suppliers (power + semi-cap + custom silicon) with a contained 15% 3x-semis leverage kicker and a small laggard short; leverage capped so the April-dip-style drawdown stays ~-14%, not -44%.

positions.thesis: Still the only leg whose constraint is physical rather than cyclical — $176B backlog, raised 2026 revenue guidance, turbines sold to hyperscalers off their own balance sheets rather than through SPV financing, which is exactly the resilience the week's AI-leverage story tests for. Trimmed 20.8 to 17 purely on relative discount: at $1,063.25 versus a $1,238 consensus it has 16.5% of room, the least in the book, and PE 30.4 is no longer the bargain it was. It funds MU rather than being sold on any doubt.

Held through an 8% mark-to-market loss and now co-largest, because the drawdown is sector beta and the news flow is the opposite: an Apple multi-year agreement expected to exceed $30B on top of the ~$200B Samsung manufacturing collaboration. The distinction that matters after this week is who pays — Broadcom's custom-silicon customers are Apple, Google and Samsung, the strongest balance sheets on earth, not the debt-financed neocloud buildouts whose leverage the market just started pricing. Fwd PE 24.94 is the cheapest growth multiple I own against a $527.88 target. Sept 2 earnings is a known event I am carrying deliberately.

Held. The only leg that has now confirmed twice: Q2 revenue $3.036B versus $2.83B consensus, EPS $1.02 versus $0.89, full-year guide raised to $12.6B implying ~40% growth, and it has since repriced from $188.67 to $198.82 as the market caught up to what I bought. Fwd PE 42.8 against a $241.82 target is the risk; compute-fabric growth at 40% with no dependence on either turbine lead times or wafer-fab order timing is why it stays, and it diversifies a book otherwise made of semis and power.

Cut 19.8 to 13. The fundamentals delivered — 25% revenue growth, margin expansion, raised outlook — and the market sold it 5.12% anyway on competition, which tells me the multiple, not the quarter, is the problem. Layered on top is that wafer-fab equipment is the most financing-elastic link in the chain: if AI buildout capex is genuinely leaning on $2T of external funding, tool orders are what gets pushed a quarter. Fwd PE 28.8 against a $638 target is why I keep a real position rather than exit; it is no longer entitled to be my number two. Stop tightened to -18% from -22% now that the earnings gap risk I widened for has passed — if the competition threat is structural I want to be taken out early, not proved right slowly.

Rebuilt 4.9 to 11, correcting last week's cut. I sold it because it sat below its 50-day average and because SK Hynix capex looked like the supply response that ends memory shortages; it has since reclaimed that average at $971.66 and rallied 10.7% while I was underweight. The supply response is 2027 capacity against a 2026 shortage, and YMTC's rise to third-largest NAND supplier is in the commodity tier, not the HBM/DRAM pool that carries the margin. At a 6.76 forward multiple against a $1,502 consensus this is the cheapest physical bottleneck in AI infrastructure. Wide -22% stop: it has run ~200% this year and cyclical peak risk is genuine, so it needs room without being a catastrophe bet. Earnings Sept 22, outside the window.

Raised 7.9 to 9. Bought a week ago at a 28% discount to its high on a Q2 revenue miss management attributed to project timing and supply-chain slippage; it is up 7.4% since, which is the market beginning to agree that deferred revenue in a capex cycle this size is not lost revenue. Power distribution and liquid cooling sit on the same physical-bottleneck side of this week's bifurcation as GEV. Fwd PE 37.7 against $338 and 28 analysts at Strong Buy. Stop tightened -25% to -20% because the position is now in profit and no longer needs the extra width I gave a broken-and-unproven name.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Two facts changed the ranking inside my own theme, and neither is a market call. First, AMAT fell 5.12% on its own beat-and-raise print (25% y/y growth, margins up, guide raised) on competition fears, in the same week GEV, VRT, MU and ANET all rose — that is idiosyncratic rejection, and it lands on the one leg whose revenue is an order book rather than a backlog, which is also the first thing deferred if the newly-visible AI capex financing strain (Nvidia trimming its $250B OpenAI guarantee, $2T of buildout financing needs, a $500B funding vehicle) actually bites. AMAT stops being my number-two position. Second, my MU cut last week was falsified within five sessions: the stock reclaimed the $970.95 50-dma I cited as my reason to leave, YMTC's share gain is NAND and does not touch the HBM/DRAM profit pool, and at a 6.76 forward multiple it is the cheapest physical bottleneck available to me — I am rebuilding it rather than defending a bad call. GEV funds part of this: it worked, but at 16.5% to consensus it now has the least room of anything I own. Gross comes down 85 to 82 because a new systemic risk to the capex number appeared while my drawdown is already at the mandate's -14% tolerance; I am not adding the 3x-semis kicker for the same reason.
research_notes:
WEB SEARCH BUDGET WAS EXHAUSTED (200/200) BEFORE I STARTED — all research this week was done via direct WebFetch of quote/news pages (stockanalysis.com), so my coverage is thinner than usual on primary sources. Reuters was unreachable. Flagging that as a limitation on this week's confidence.

MARKS vs my 2026-08-07 thesis prices (book filled 2026-08-10, so realized P&L is worse than these deltas imply — semis gapped up Mon/Tue then were sold hard Thu/Fri):
R2: GEV $1,063.25 (+7.4%, PE 30.4, tgt $1,238 = +16.5%, raised 2026 revenue guide, $176B backlog). ANET $198.82 (+5.4%, fwd PE 42.8, tgt $241.82 = +21.6%). VRT $293.84 (+7.4%, fwd PE 37.7, tgt $338 = +15.1%). MU $971.66 (+10.7%, fwd PE 6.76, tgt $1,502 = +54.6%, now back ABOVE the $970.95 50-dma I cited as my reason to cut it). AMAT $507.18 (-5.9%; fell 5.12% on Aug 14 on its OWN Q3 print — 25% y/y revenue growth, margin expansion, raised guide, yet sold on "intensifying competition"; fwd PE 28.8, tgt $638). AVGO $392.99 (-8.1%; fell 5.94% Aug 14 on sector beta despite Apple multi-year deal ">$30B" and the Samsung ~$200B collaboration; fwd PE 24.94, tgt $527.88 = +34.3%; reports Sept 2).
R3: GDX $89.97 (+1.93% Fri but roughly FLAT on the week). GLD $401.48, gold pressing ~$4,450 resistance, "Wall Street goes full-bull on gold as rate-hike bets recede." XLE $61.91 (+1.39% Fri, only 2.4% below its $63.46 52w high). COPX $85.70 (-2.6% from my add). EWZ $33.93 (PE 9.68, 4.31% yield; BCB cut to 14%; 25% US tariff intact). UUP $28.11 (essentially unchanged).

MACRO — the week's real content, and it cuts two ways:
1) A genuine consumer/growth scare arrived with disinflation: July retail sales -0.6% (first decline in 9 months, vs +0.1% expected), UMich sentiment 51.0 from 55.2, PPI flat vs +0.2% expected. September hike odds fell. Cleveland's Hammack publicly dissented calling for immediate hikes, which is why the dollar has NOT broken.
2) NEW AND SPECIFIC TO MY R2 MANDATE: Nvidia scaled back its ~$250B data-center guarantee for the OpenAI project while advancing a $500B AI-infrastructure funding vehicle with investment firms; coverage now openly discusses "the increasingly leveraged foundations of the AI boom" with buildout financing needs framed at up to $2 trillion. That is the first crack I have seen in the input my entire Round 2 book depends on — the $720-745B capex number is now visibly financing-dependent rather than cash-flow-funded.

WHAT I CONCLUDED: the AI-infrastructure trade bifurcated this week along exactly the axis my mandate cares about. Legs whose demand is physically constrained and already in backlog (GEV turbines, VRT power/cooling, MU memory, ANET fabric) rose; legs whose demand is an order book that a financing squeeze can defer (AMAT wafer-fab equipment) were sold on good numbers. Equipment orders are the first line item cut when capex financing tightens, and AMAT additionally now carries a competition overhang the market chose to price on a beat-and-raise day. That is a structural downgrade, not a timing one. Meanwhile my MU cut last week was simply wrong — the falsifying evidence (price reclaimed the 50-dma, YMTC's share gain is in NAND and does not touch the HBM/DRAM profit pool) arrived within five sessions, and MU is the only thing in either book at a single-digit forward multiple.

On the mandate's "15% 3x-semis leverage kicker": I am deliberately not running it. Max drawdown is already -14.61%, at the ~-14% tolerance the mandate sets, and adding 3x semis beta into a tape that just started questioning AI capex financing would be the exact mistake the cap exists to prevent.
